content.content:
1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection. 1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106 is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the sensor and pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18	
19	At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution.
22	
23	At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.
24	
25	At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel. A connector channel whose measured connector current is at or below its assigned current limit has complied. A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel, that is, a further current limit lower than the limit previously assigned to it, and repeats the verification. This is a first stage of the reduction of the allocation, continued at the staged reduction step 210 described below, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.
26	
27	At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.
28	
29	At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
30	
31	The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.
32	
33	At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.
34	
35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.
36	
37	The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.
38	
39	During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.
40	
41	Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.
42	
43	The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.
44	
45	The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time.
46	
47	The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling.
48	
49	The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.
50

A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. It may follow a reduced limit after a delay, may follow it in coarse steps, or may not follow it. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, and holds the tamper-evident local sequence of meter records described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118, or a lagging response by a vehicle, does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller. Distribution of the remainder in proportion to the stored energy-deficit values is one implementation of this distribution.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel. A connector channel whose measured connector current is at or below its assigned current limit has complied. A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel, that is, a further current limit lower than the limit previously assigned to it, and repeats the verification. This is a first stage of the reduction of the allocation, continued at the staged reduction step 210 described below, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval. The verification interval is a stored period long enough to allow a vehicle that is going to obey the reduced pilot command to do so, and is the period within which a compliant installation resolves an overcurrent by signalling alone.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. A trip of the branch overcurrent device would end every charging session on the branch at the same instant and would also remove the non-charging load 118, and would require a manual reset at the distribution equipment before any session could resume. Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel identifies which connector channel is not honouring its assigned current limit, so that the reduced pilot command can be directed at that connector channel first. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the only input that authorizes the opening of a contactor. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened when the branch is in fact within its limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

data.summary:
Reviewed input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md (identical text), all eleven draft sections, draft/numerals.md, and the four figure briefs. Two workspace conditions limited the review and are stated plainly: (a) figures/ contains only FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md — there are no rendered-*.png images and no review/figure-audit-evidence.json, so no pixel, OCR, leader or endpoint verification was possible and figure review was confined to agreement between each brief, numerals.md and the specification (the absent sheets are already covered by the mechanical "described figure has a drawing sheet" failure and are not re-reported); (b) prior_art/INDEX.md lists "(none)" and the draft contains no [REF:...] citation, so citation fidelity is vacuous — nothing is characterised that a source could contradict, and the art given to this draft may be incomplete.

On the material checked the draft is largely faithful. The core claim chain traces to exact disclosure passages: the four stored per-session values, the allocation-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve, minimum-sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector-sensor verification, the verification interval after a reduced pilot command, ordered one-at-a-time shedding until branch current is below the limit, the three reclosure conditions, the leakage-threshold welded-contactor record with inhibition of the other contactors and the local fault indicator, offline continuation under the last accepted branch limit, non-start of new sessions without an unexpired signed local token, and the service-input commissioning map confirmed at the sensing channel. All 27 numerals in numerals.md are used in the detailed description, each labels one part only, and each appears in exactly one figure brief in a consistent role (100/102/104/106/108/118/120/140 on FIG. 1; 108/120/122/124/126/128/130 on FIG. 2; 106/110/112/114/116/132/134 on FIG. 3; 202-216 on FIG. 4). The Brief Description of the Drawings matches what each brief depicts, no figure is said to show something its brief omits, and the FIG. 4 flow (diamond 210 with a return to 202, column to 212/214/216, terminator on the welded branch) matches the described operation. The abstract is 146 words. The claim-word warning is a false positive: the only "missing" token is the word "claim" from dependent-claim references. The three defects reported in review/previous-qa.md have all been corrected in the current text.

Eight defects are reported: one added allocation rule the disclosure does not state, one added claim-recited storage location, one logic gap where the described branch-overcurrent response has no defined action in a case the draft itself contemplates, an added bus connection to the connector current sensor that also appears in the FIG. 2 brief, three unsourced characterisations, and one claim/description name drift for the same element. Each has a local, source-supported fix in the existing text or figure brief.

findings.title: The staged reduction step has no defined action when branch current is above the limit and no connector channel was identified as non-compliant
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 27 (staged reduction step 210)
findings.detail: Step 210 is entered whenever the measured branch current exceeds the branch current limit. The described response sends the reduced pilot command to a connector channel "identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit". The draft itself expressly contemplates the case where no such channel exists: paragraph 19 says the reserve exists so that "a step in the non-charging load 118 ... does not by itself carry the branch above its limit", and paragraph 31 says the branch sensor "states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report". In that case — every connector channel at or below its assigned limit, branch over the limit because the non-charging load rose — step 210 as written has no channel to address, so the verification interval that gates ordered shedding at step 212 is started by a command the text gives no recipient for. Claim 1 does not carry the "identified channel" restriction (it is added by claim 2), so the broader claim covers a case the description does not walk through. A source-supported action exists and only needs stating: the disclosure's allocation loop already subtracts the measured non-charging branch load at each allocation interval, so a risen non-charging load lowers the available charging current and hence every assigned limit at the next interval.

Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md line 27): "When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval."

findings.fix: In the paragraph at line 27, replace "the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, and starts a verification interval." with "the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval. Where a connector channel has been identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit, the edge controller 106 directs the reduced pilot command to that connector channel. Where no connector channel has been so identified, the reduced pilot command is the lower assigned current limit that the available current determination step 202 produces at the next allocation interval from the increased measured non-charging branch load."
